title: Lockout/Tagout for Centrifugal Pumps
body:
1. Obtain a signed work permit from the Unit Operator before any isolation begins.
2. Verify the pump is de-energized at the local disconnect and at MCC-3, breaker position confirmed OPEN by a qualified electrician.
3. Apply a personal lock and danger tag at both the local disconnect and the MCC breaker. Each craftsperson applies their own lock; group lockboxes require the Authorized Employee to hold the key.
4. Close and lock suction and discharge block valves. Chain-and-lock is acceptable where handwheel locking is not practical.
5. Bleed the casing to the closed drain header through the 3/4-inch drain valve. Verify zero pressure on the local gauge AND by cracking the vent, a gauge reading alone is not acceptable verification.
6. Attempt-to-start test: with locks applied, attempt to start from the local station and from the DCS. Confirm no rotation.
7. Record isolation points on the LOTO log (Form HSE-22) and attach to the permit.
RELEASE: Reverse in order. The person who applied a lock is the only person authorized to remove it, except under the documented Lock Removal exception requiring Area Supervisor and HSE Manager signature.

title: Confined Space Entry. Vessels and Columns
body:
1. A Confined Space Entry Permit (Form HSE-07) must be issued by the Entry Supervisor and is valid for one shift only.
2. Isolation: vessel must be blinded, not merely valved. Double block and bleed is NOT sufficient for entry, a positive blind or physical disconnect is required.
3. Purge: nitrogen purge to displace hydrocarbon, then AIR purge to restore breathable atmosphere. Entry on a nitrogen-inert atmosphere is prohibited without supplied air and rescue standby.
4. Atmospheric testing before entry, by a qualified Gas Tester, in this order: oxygen (19.5-23.5%), flammability (<10% LEL), toxics (H2S <10 ppm, benzene <0.5 ppm).
5. Continuous monitoring during occupancy. Test at multiple elevations, heavier-than-air vapors stratify at the bottom.
6. An Attendant remains outside the space at all times with continuous communication and a means to summon rescue. The Attendant performs no other duties.
7. Retrieval equipment (harness + tripod) required for vertical entries over 5 feet.
EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY on any alarm, loss of ventilation, loss of communication, or unplanned change in conditions.
notes: Rev 12 tightened the blinding requirement. Rev 11 and earlier permitted double-block-and-bleed; do not cite those revisions.

title: Hot Work Permitting
body:
1. Hot Work Permit (Form HSE-11) required for any spark-producing work outside a designated safe area. Valid for one shift, maximum 12 hours.
2. Combustible gas test within 30 minutes of starting work, and at least every 2 hours during work. Result must be 0% LEL.
3. Clear or protect combustibles within 35 feet. Cover drains and sewers within 35 feet.
4. A dedicated Fire Watch is required during work and for 60 minutes after work stops. The Fire Watch performs no other duties and has an extinguisher and a means of alarm.
5. Hot work is prohibited during a unit upset, during a flare outage, or when the facility is on Level 2 weather standby.
6. Notify the Control Room before starting and immediately on completion.

title: Mechanical Seal Replacement, API 682 Dual Pressurized
body:
PREREQUISITE: SOP-LOTO-014 isolation complete and verified. Do not begin seal work on an unverified isolation.
1. Depressurize and drain the seal support system (Plan 53B accumulator) to the barrier fluid recovery drum. Bleed nitrogen from the bladder side to 0 psig.
2. Record as-found barrier fluid level, pressure, and any discoloration on the work order. Discolored barrier fluid indicates inboard seal leakage, flag to Reliability before proceeding.
3. Remove the coupling guard and coupling. Record shaft runout with a dial indicator; runout above 0.002 inch TIR requires Reliability sign-off before reassembly.
4. Remove the gland bolting in a star pattern. Support the cartridge, do not let it hang on the shaft.
5. Inspect the shaft sleeve and seal chamber bore for fretting. Fretting deeper than 0.005 inch requires shaft replacement, not polishing.
6. Install the replacement cartridge dry. Do not lubricate the faces with anything other than the OEM-specified fluid, hydrocarbon on the faces will cause blistering on the carbon.
7. Set the cartridge clips per the OEM drawing, torque the gland to the values in Table 4, and only then remove the setting clips.
8. Recharge the barrier fluid system and pressurize to 25 psig above the higher of suction or seal chamber pressure.
9. Bump test, verify no leakage, then release to Operations with a completed Form MNT-14.

title: Line Breaking and Blinding
body:
1. Line Break Permit (Form HSE-19) required for any opening of process equipment or piping that has contained hazardous material.
2. Identify the contents and hazards from the Line List and current SDS. If contents are unknown, treat as the worst credible case for the unit.
3. Isolate, depressurize, and drain to a closed system. Verify zero energy at a low-point drain AND a high-point vent.
4. Required PPE at minimum: chemical splash suit, face shield over safety glasses, chemical-resistant gloves. Add supplied-air respiratory protection for H2S service or where benzene exposure is credible.
5. Position personnel out of the line of fire. Loosen the flange bolting on the far side first, breaking the gasket away from the body.
6. Install blinds per the blind list and record on the Blind Register. Every blind installed must be logged for removal.
7. Hydrocarbon or H2S service requires a standing gas monitor at the work face for the duration of the break.

title: Tank Gauging and Level Verification
body:
1. Automatic Tank Gauging (ATG) is the primary level indication. Manual gauging is required weekly for custody-transfer tanks and any time ATG is in doubt.
2. Manual gauging on a floating-roof tank requires the roof to be off the legs and the gauge hatch to be opened slowly to relieve any pressure.
3. Ground the gauge tape to the gauge hatch before lowering to prevent static ignition. Wait 30 seconds after grounding.
4. Do not gauge during a lightning advisory or within 30 minutes of the start of a receipt into that tank, turbulence invalidates the reading.
5. Compare manual to ATG. A discrepancy greater than 1/4 inch requires a re-gauge; a repeat discrepancy is an ATG work request.
6. High-high level alarm testing is quarterly and is a separate procedure (SOP-OPS-056). Do not rely on gauging to demonstrate overfill protection.
notes: Overfill protection is governed by API 2350. Tank 42 is in Category 3 service.

title: Hydrogen Sulfide Exposure Response
body:
H2S is immediately dangerous to life or health at 100 ppm. It deadens the sense of smell, absence of odor is NOT evidence of absence of gas.
1. On personal monitor alarm (10 ppm): stop work, move crosswind and upwind, notify the Control Room.
2. On high alarm (15 ppm) or area alarm: evacuate to the designated muster point, account for all personnel.
3. DO NOT attempt rescue without supplied-air respiratory protection and a standby person. Would-be rescuers are the most common second casualty.
4. Move a casualty to fresh air only if you can do so without exposing yourself. Begin rescue breathing with a barrier device if not breathing; H2S casualties can recover fully with prompt oxygen.
5. All exposures, including alarms with no symptoms, require a report to HSE within the shift and a medical evaluation.
Emergency number: plant radio Channel 1 or extension 5555.

title: Electrical Work in Classified Areas
body:
1. Determine the area classification from the Electrical Area Classification drawings before selecting tools or equipment. Do not assume.
2. Only intrinsically safe or explosion-proof rated equipment may be energized in Class I Division 1 and Division 2 areas.
3. Non-rated test equipment, cameras, and personal electronics require a Hot Work Permit even where no spark-producing work is planned.
4. Opening an explosion-proof enclosure on live equipment is prohibited. De-energize and verify absence of voltage per SOP-LOTO-014.
5. All enclosure covers must be reinstalled with the full complement of bolts and the flame path clean and undamaged. A missing bolt defeats the rating.
6. Arc flash PPE per the equipment label. If the label is missing or illegible, treat as Category 4 until an engineering study confirms otherwise.
